Extract NAT_DATA layers into a Where To Work project

Source: R/wtw.R
extract_wtw_natdata.Rd

Extracts the layers of a NAT_DATA folder (ConsTech's shared national data) for a Where To Work (WTW) project's planning units, and writes them to the project's tifs folder: natdata_template() and extract_layers() with the NAT_DATA catalogue (read_natdata_metadata()), each layer written with its catalogue prefix, data type and folder. It is wtw-data-prep2's step 03 in one call, and the defaults write the files that step writes, except aoi/pu_1km_align.tif, written only when align_file asks for it.

Usage

extract_wtw_natdata(
  natdata_dir,
  project_dir,
  aoi_raster = file.path(project_dir, "aoi", "pu_1km.tif"),
  layers = read_natdata_metadata(natdata_dir),
  tifs_dir = "tifs",
  align_file = NULL,
  align_value = 1,
  align_datatype = "INT1U",
  align_name = "layer",
  round_int = TRUE,
  multiband = FALSE,
  drop_empty = TRUE,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  progress = function(i, n, layer) {
    
    cli::cli_inform("Layer {i} of {n}: {basename(layer)}")
 },
  template_file = "_1km/idx.tif"
)

Arguments

natdata_dir

The NAT_DATA folder: a single path to an existing folder, such as a dated release (NAT_DATA_20261009). Its template, the file template_file, is opened with natdata_template() and, by default, its catalogue read with read_natdata_metadata(). Where NAT_DATA lives is each tool's own setting; this function only reads from it.

project_dir

The WTW project folder: a single folder path, under which tifs_dir (and align_file) are written. Missing folders, project_dir included, are created. Where the project lives is each tool's own setting.

aoi_raster

The planning units as a raster, on the template's grid, either a path to a raster file or a SpatRaster with one layer. Every cell that is not NA is a planning unit, whatever its value, and its extent is the extent of every file written. The default is the project's aoi/pu_1km.tif, as create_wtw_planning_units() writes it; the aoi_raster that function returns gives the same files.

layers

The layers to extract: a data frame with a file column of full file paths and, optionally, prefix, datatype and subdir columns for each layer, as read_natdata_metadata() returns. The default is the active layers of natdata_dir's catalogue; pass some of its rows to extract only those layers. Other columns are ignored, and a vector of file paths also works (see extract_layers()).

tifs_dir

The folder the layers are written to, as a path relative to project_dir. The default, "tifs", is the WTW project layout.

align_file

NULL (the default) or the file to write the planning units to on the template's full grid, as a path relative to project_dir. wtw-data-prep2's step 03 wrote "aoi/pu_1km_align.tif"; no WTW step reads it, so it is not written unless asked for.

align_value

A single finite number, the value of the planning units in align_file. The default, 1, is wtw-data-prep2's. Ignored without align_file.

align_datatype

The data type of align_file, one of terra's data types (see terra::writeRaster()). The default, "INT1U", is wtw-data-prep2's. align_value must be a value it stores: for an integer type, a whole number after rounding (halves away from zero) within the type's range and not its NoData value (for example 0 to 254 for "INT1U"). Ignored without align_file.

align_name

A single, non-empty string, the name of the one band (layer) of align_file, as terra reads it back with names(). The default, "layer", is wtw-data-prep2's. Ignored without align_file.

round_int

A single logical, passed to write_rasters(): TRUE (the default) rounds values to whole numbers, halves away from zero, before writing them as an integer type; FALSE lets terra cut the decimals off. Float types are never rounded.

multiband

A single logical: FALSE (the default) writes one file per feature, as wtw-data-prep2 does; TRUE writes one multi-band file per layer, named after the layer's file (see extract_layers()).

drop_empty

A single logical: TRUE (the default) drops the features with no values in the AOI (every value 0 or NA), as clip_rij_matrix() does, and skips a layer left with none, naming them in a message; FALSE keeps every feature, so a feature absent from the AOI gives a raster of 0s.

overwrite

A single logical: TRUE (the default) replaces existing files, as wtw-data-prep2 does; FALSE stops with an error if a file to write exists, checked before extracting for every file that can be named then.

progress

NULL for no progress messages, or a function called before each layer is extracted as progress(i, n, layer), with the layer's number i, the number of layers n and the layer's path layer. The default prints a short message naming the layer, since a national extraction can take a while.

template_file

The template's file within natdata_dir, as a path relative to it, passed to natdata_template() as its file. The default, "_1km/idx.tif", is NAT_DATA's national template. Another path opens a template kept elsewhere in the folder, such as another version or resolution of the grid.

Value

The paths of the layer files written, invisibly: a character vector in the order written, named after the feature (or, with multiband = TRUE, after the layer's file name without its extension). align_file, when written, is not among them.

Method

  1. Template: natdata_template() opens template_file in natdata_dir, by default _1km/idx.tif, the national grid of 1 km cells in Canada_Albers_WGS_1984; only which of its cells have data is used.

  2. Layers: extract_layers() with path_column = "file", one layer at a time, in the order of layers: each layer is read as an rij matrix (a GeoTIFF on the template's grid, or an .rds rij matrix), clipped to the planning units (the cells of aoi_raster that are not NA and where the template has data, matched by position on the shared grid) and rebuilt as one raster per feature on aoi_raster's extent: the feature's values in the planning units, 0 where it has none, NA elsewhere. Raster, not vector, operations: nothing is resampled and no areas are computed.

  3. Writing: to <project_dir>/<tifs_dir>/<subdir>/<prefix><feature>.tif, with each layer's prefix, datatype and subdir from layers (in NAT_DATA's catalogue, subdir is the layer's folder). With round_int = TRUE, values are rounded halves away from zero before an integer data type. With drop_empty = TRUE, features with no values in the planning units are not written, and layers left with none are skipped, each named in a message.

  4. Aligned planning units (only with align_file), after the layers: a raster of align_value in the planning units and NA elsewhere, one layer named align_name, put on the template's full grid with align_raster() (nearest neighbour) and written in align_datatype, NA as terra's NoData value for it. The defaults, 1 as INT1U (NoData 255) in a layer named layer, are wtw-data-prep2's pu_1km_align.tif.

Arguments, aoi_raster, the template and the output files that can be named in advance are checked before any layer is read (see extract_layers()). If a layer fails, the error names it, and the files of the layers before it are kept.

With the defaults, the files are those of wtw-data-prep2's step 03 (natdata()): the same names, folders, data types, NoData values, extents and values. Intended changes from it: aoi/pu_1km_align.tif is not written unless align_file names it, empty features and layers are named in messages, and problems are found before extracting where they can be. Decisions are recorded in ADR 0015, ADR 0016 and ADR 0020.

See also

create_wtw_planning_units(), which writes aoi/pu_1km.tif; extract_layers(), read_natdata_metadata() and natdata_template(), which it calls.

Other wtw: create_dataprep_template(), create_wtw_planning_units(), create_wtw_project_folder(), dataprep_columns(), wtw_project_folders()

Examples

# A small NAT_DATA-like folder: a 10 x 10 template and a catalogue of
# three active layers (cover.tif is a GeoTIFF, which needs prioritizr)
natdata_dir <- system.file("extdata", "natdata", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
project_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "wtw_natdata")

if (requireNamespace("prioritizr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # Step 02 writes aoi/pu_1km.tif; step 03 extracts the layers for it
  pu <- create_wtw_planning_units(aoi, natdata_dir, project_dir)
  paths <- extract_wtw_natdata(natdata_dir, project_dir)
  list.files(file.path(project_dir, "tifs"), recursive = TRUE)

  # The raster step 02 returns gives the same files; here only the
  # species layer, without progress messages
  layers <- read_natdata_metadata(natdata_dir)
  paths <- extract_wtw_natdata(
    natdata_dir, project_dir,
    aoi_raster = pu$aoi_raster,
    layers = layers[layers$file_name == "features.rds", ],
    progress = NULL
  )
  basename(paths)

  # Also write the planning units on the template's full grid
  paths <- extract_wtw_natdata(
    natdata_dir, project_dir,
    align_file = "aoi/pu_1km_align.tif", progress = NULL
  )
  terra::rast(file.path(project_dir, "aoi", "pu_1km_align.tif"))

  # The same file with the planning units as 0s, in a signed data type,
  # in a band named "pu"
  paths <- extract_wtw_natdata(
    natdata_dir, project_dir,
    align_file = "aoi/pu_1km_align.tif", align_value = 0,
    align_datatype = "INT2S", align_name = "pu", progress = NULL
  )
  terra::rast(file.path(project_dir, "aoi", "pu_1km_align.tif"))
}
